sources.publisher: Ministerio de Obras Públicas, Gobierno de Chile
sources.type: Primary basin-planning report, its own hydrographic map and bounded supporting synthesis
sources.actually_inspected: Cover/front-matter; printed pages4–8,12–17; Figures2.1,2.2,2.3 and2.5 (PDF pages23,25,28,35). Figure2.5 and the acquired MMA source form the principal geographic correspondence evidence.
sources.principal_original_map: Figure2.5, Delimitación de unidades hidrográficas de la zona de la Pampa del Tamarugal, printed page17: credited elaboración propia, with WGS84 UTM19S grid, 40km scale bar, mapped quebradas, relief, distinct salar polygons and labels for Salar de Pintados and Salar de Bella Vista.
sources.supports: Full regional head-to-pampa-to-salar setting; the southward drainage beside/into the Pintados–Bellavista saline depression; the selected endpoint within the Bellavista terminal salar setting. Report text identifies the basin as endorheic, describes alluvial-fan termination and infiltration of usual streamflow, with occasional exceptional runoff.
sources.cartographic_attribution: Figure2.1 is the report authors’ basin/subbasin delimitation, partly DEM-based; basin boundaries are used only for context, never as proof of a river connection. Figure2.2 is explicitly modified from SERNAGEOMIN2017. Figure2.3 is a geological compilation from cited maps and SERNAGEOMIN2017. These supplementary figures show regional geomorphology and saline deposits; no standalone underlying geological publication was acquired or claimed independently inspected.
sources.prose_attribution: Printed page16 cites earlier DGA/CIDERH literature for the distinction between upper perennial reaches and lower infiltration. This is the successfully read2021 report’s synthesis, not a claim to have acquired those older originals. Printed pages6–8 independently explain the report’s endorheic basin and fan setting; pages12–13 explain the mapped saline-deposit class.
sources.limits: The report’s model/basin delineations and groundwater flow are not treated as surface-channel continuity. Neither Figure2.5 nor prose establishes a single river hydronym for the northeastern unnamed branch plus every pampa/salar passage. Generalized cartography is used at corridor/component scale, without current wetness or precise shoreline claims.
sources.distinct_publication: Precisely identified April2021 Pampa del Tamarugal report, separate from stopped Loa/DGA2014 figures, current Vialidad portal and Codelco Pedernales2023. Unresolved historical MOP/DGA/Loa/CIREN references remain preserved; no blanket clearance or domain-wide ban was inferred.
sources.use_notice: Front-matter supplies a recommended bibliographic citation for the joint Lluta/Pampa study, SIT473. No distribution restriction was observed in the inspected pages; government hosting is not treated as redistribution permission. Originals and derivative orientation figures remain private.

correspondence.finding: The selected start corresponds to the mapped channel in the Batalha–Cachoeira–Caiana setting north of São Bento do Una. It runs east/northeast toward the Riachão and Riachão de Igrejinha localities. The complete selected western corridor is visible on the São Bento map, including the approach to the overlap with Cachoeirinha; no source-spring identity or initial-segment hydronym is imposed.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary corridor scale

correspondence.finding: The connected northern watercourse is explicitly labelled Riacho Riachão around Riachão de Igrejinha/Capim de Planeta. The Cachoeirinha sheet follows it east through the Cabanas setting, around the northward bend and south toward the Una approach west of Cachoeirinha. The selected route continues through the city setting and eastward. The separately mapped Una approach from the southwest is distinguished from this selected feeder.
correspondence.correspondence: complete; exact name-transition point not assigned

correspondence.finding: The state original supplies the continuous eastward river corridor from Cachoeirinha toward Altinho and the Agrestina/São Joaquim do Monte setting, then southeast past the Laje Grande/Bonito-side valley toward Palmares. It distinguishes the parallel Ipojuca and Sirinhaém rivers and the southern Rio da Chata/Pirangi drainage; these nearby labels are not transferred to the selected Una trunk.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at regional corridor scale; prose contextual only

correspondence.component_scope: Serro Azul reservoir and Palmares reach
correspondence.finding: The 2022 original visibly shows the expanded reservoir beside Usina Serro Azul, its dam/outlet and the connected downstream Rio Una. This matches the selected west-to-east approach and subsequent southward bend toward Palmares. The Rio da Prata approach and the Pirangi-side tributary drainage remain separate from the selected trunk. The earlier 2020 map preserves generalized river continuity; its narrower water depiction does not replace the reservoir observation.
correspondence.correspondence: complete including the major reservoir passage

correspondence.finding: The original state map shows the Una leaving Palmares through the Água Preta lowlands, turning toward the coastal reach north of Barreiros, and distinguishes the Jacuípe tributary to the south. The Barreiros map supplies the expanded lower reach with mapped islands and river bends through the Barreiros vicinity before the estuary.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary corridor scale

correspondence.finding: The Barreiros original carries the Una from the town’s river bends toward Várzea do Una and its opening to the Atlantic. The separately labelled Rio Carimã approaches from the west/southwest and is distinguished from the selected Una trunk. The São José da Coroa Grande sheet independently shows the Carimã/coastal approach south of the mouth, but was not counted as complete Una-mouth coverage. The actual selected sea-terminal setting is established by the Barreiros and state originals, without a bank-by-bank or exact endpoint audit.
correspondence.correspondence: complete terminal correspondence

correspondence.component_scope: Northeastern head and initial westward branch
correspondence.finding: The detailed official map contains the selected head and westward channel sequence, then its bend southwest into the upper Tarapacá network. The head is in the mountainous northeastern basin setting shown by the2021 report. Labels on separate nearby northern/eastern joining branches do not establish a name for this selected head.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at generalized head/branch corridor scale; head hydronym remains null

correspondence.component_scope: Upper confluence and westward Tarapacá corridor
correspondence.finding: The mapped selected branch joins the westward corridor carrying repeated Quebrada de Tarapacá labels. Its bends and junction setting are supported by the official original head and overview maps. Neighboring labeled branches are orientation context, not additional selected tributaries or name transfers.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at corridor/junction scale

correspondence.component_scope: Middle Tarapacá canyon and piedmont exit
correspondence.finding: The selected westward-to-southwestward route corresponds to the mapped Tarapacá valley north of the Linga/Choja and Coscaya drainage setting, then enters the central depression east/southeast of Huara. The report maps its mountain-to-pampa transition.
correspondence.correspondence: complete; no precise-bank or vertex agreement claim

correspondence.component_scope: Long southward alluvial-pampa continuation toward Pozo Almonte
correspondence.finding: The official sources depict southward drainage in the central depression through the Pozo Almonte corridor, with Quebrada de Tarapacá labels on the mapped eastern line and Quebrada Salar de Pintados on a distinct western line. The selected generalized line passes through this alluvial-pampa setting; it is not inferred to be a continuously flowing river. Report prose explains fan and infiltration behavior.
correspondence.correspondence: complete geographic setting, including generalized offsets across mapped alluvial terrain

correspondence.component_scope: Pintados saline-depression approach and eastern-side passage
correspondence.finding: The selected continuation passes the drainage convergence south of Pozo Almonte and follows the eastern Pintados saline-depression setting. Figure2.5 explicitly distinguishes the salar polygon from quebrada lines; the report geology map identifies broad saline deposits. A salar name is not a river name and no selected lake or reservoir passage is asserted.
correspondence.correspondence: complete pampa/salar component coverage

correspondence.component_scope: Pintados–Bellavista transition and Chacarilla joining setting
correspondence.finding: Both original map sources show the southward drainage and eastward Quebrada de Chacarilla/O del Salado joining setting between Pintados and Bellavista. Figure2.5 maps the enclosing saline lowland and intervening terrain. This is an observed geographic transition, not evidence that groundwater flow or modeled connectivity creates one continuously named river.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at inter-salar corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: Final southern tail and endorheic terminal
correspondence.finding: The final selected tail extends beyond the southern end of the MMA hydrographic line. The2021 original Figure2.5 nevertheless covers the full tail and endpoint within the Bellavista saline terminal setting. The regional geomorphology and saline-deposit maps corroborate the lowland/salar surface. The final westward curl is not established as a named stream or open-water lake channel.
correspondence.correspondence: complete terminal terrain coverage; completed naming-scope hold rather than an unviewed-connector gap
correspondence.mapped_setting_name: Salar de Bellavista (map label: Salar de Bella Vista)

correspondence.finding: Long east-to-west Rupumeica corridor joins the separately named Hueinahue before its entry into southeastern Maihue. Selected passage crosses Maihue, follows the short Calcurrupe outlet corridor, then crosses Ranco westward. The river names are not extended across either lake. The small initial north/south hooked branch east of the well-mapped Rupumeica remains geographically unaccounted for, despite primary prose placing the river origin near the frontier cordillera/Portezuelo Lago Hermoso setting.

correspondence.unresolved_material_gap: Initial hooked headward branch before the recognizable westbound Rupumeica corridor. Available primary line cartography does not show it, and no usable terrain/source map establishes its actual start and connection. This is not merely an unknown local hydronym.

correspondence.finding: Western Ranco passage and its western outlet transition; it is substantially a lake/outlet setting, not uniformly a river reach.

correspondence.finding: Ranco outlet river runs west through the central lowland/Río Bueno locality corridor; the southern Pilmaiquén branch joins before the downstream Rahue junction. The selected fragment ends at the Rahue joining setting.

correspondence.finding: Lower Bueno continues west from the Rahue confluence through the coastal valley to the Pacific mouth north of Punta Dehui. The retained source endpoint and renderer sea extension are modeled metadata, not a new mouth survey or a hydronym assigned to offshore water.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary geographic corridor scale

The2019 inspected basin figure covers this headwater drainage setting; its unnamed small streams are not all called Gaviotas. The selected route then crosses Rupanco westward and follows its Rahue outlet downstream toward the Coihueco joining setting.

correspondence.finding: Rahue continues west/northwest from the upper joining setting and ends where the south-coming Negro enters, south of Osorno.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary geographic corridor scale

correspondence.finding: Selected lower Negro starts within an existing mapped valley, rather than at the river’s natural source; it runs north from the Río Negro/Forrahue/Chifín tributary setting to join Rahue south of Osorno. It is kept separate from the Rahue outlet-lake branch.

The operator map places Pilmaiquén, Rucatayo and Los Lagos hydroelectric settings in sequence before the Chirre junction setting at the fragment end. Constancia is linked by the Bonito tributary in CONAF prose; the selected initial route is not asserted to traverse Constancia. correspondence.unresolved_material_gap: Short upper start before the mapped northeastern tributary/upper Golgol drainage. The acquired line source and small volcanic preview do not establish its actual start/connector setting; no nearby name, Constancia connection or basin membership fills that gap.

correspondence.finding: Pilmaiquén continues northwest from the Chirre receiving setting and joins the south side of Bueno, upstream of the separate Rahue confluence.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary geographic corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: Headward Timber Creek northwest of Bishopville
correspondence.finding: The selected northern beginning corresponds to the mapped Timber Creek corridor in the Timber Creek Road / Farborough Road country. It follows that creek south and then east past the Maple Branch, Long Branch and Nancy Branch junction settings toward the confluence with Black Creek. The original map labels and continuous channel establish this headward feeder; the farther-north and east Black Creek headwater network is not the selected beginning.
correspondence.correspondence: Original map pixels inspected; ordinary headward corridor correspondence supported.

correspondence.finding: Timber Creek visibly enters Black Creek west of Bishopville. The selected route follows the short southward Black Creek connector into the Cedar Creek junction setting, then the continuous wetland channel labeled Scape Ore Swamp across Camden Highway / SC 34, beneath I-20, and across the US 15 / Sumter Highway setting. Cedar Creek is an entering branch, not the selected headward continuation.
correspondence.correspondence: Material headward connectors mapped and inspected. Name-transition positions are bounded junction settings rather than exact legal endpoints.

correspondence.component_scope: Scape Ore Swamp to Black River
correspondence.finding: South of the US 15 setting, the selected line continues down mapped Scape Ore Swamp, passes the McGirts Creek junction and US 401, crosses the Florence Highway / US 76 country, and bends through the Rocky Bluff Swamp junction area. It then proceeds southeast through the broad Scape Ore wetland corridor to the separately mapped Black River near US 378. Black River approaches from the north/east; the selected route approaches along Scape Ore from the northwest.
correspondence.correspondence: Overlapping original map views cover the feeder passage and actual Black River junction; the neighboring Black River headwater is distinguished.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper Black River swamp, Dogwood Pond and Pocotaligo junction
correspondence.finding: Below the Scape Ore junction, the selected route follows the labeled Black River / Black River Swamp southeast through the I-95 and US 301 crossings and the Tearcoat Branch setting. It continues into the wide multi-channel wetland complex labeled Dogwood Pond near June Burn Road, reaches the separately mapped Pocotaligo River confluence, and bends east then northeast through the broad Black River channel-and-swamp passage toward Pudding Swamp and Chappin Swamp. The mapped river is continuous across these expansions; there is no missing lake outlet connector.
correspondence.correspondence: Original channel, wetland, pond and junction cartography inspected. SCDNR prose independently distinguishes Pocotaligo as a tributary and describes alternating broad and narrow Black River passages.

correspondence.component_scope: Kingstree and river corridor toward Andrews
correspondence.finding: The selected route turns southeast from the Pudding/Chappin swamp settings, passes the west/south side of Kingstree, crosses the US 52 / SC 261 setting, then continues south through the SC 377 crossing before bending east. It follows the meandering mapped Black River past the Boggy Swamp, Chandler Swamp and Spring Branch junction settings and the Jumping Run country toward the SC 41 crossing north of Andrews. Repeated Black River labels and the continuous mapped channel establish the middle/lower correspondence.
correspondence.correspondence: Original cartographic corridor inspected. Prose recreational-access sequence supplies bounded corroboration, not a replacement for map correspondence.

correspondence.component_scope: Andrews, lower Black River bends and Black Mingo junction
correspondence.finding: After the SC 41 / Andrews setting, the selected line follows Black River east through Horse Pen Swamp and the wider Black River Swamp corridor, past the Big Dam Swamp junction. It makes the characteristic northward lower-river bend, reaches the Black Mingo Creek junction in the Mingo Swamp / Browns Ferry Road country, crosses the SC 51 setting, and continues through the broad southeastward bends past Choppee Creek, Peters Creek and the US 701 crossing. These are river and wetland passages, not a selected reservoir crossing.
correspondence.correspondence: Overlapping original map views cover the major lower bends and material tributary junctions.

correspondence.component_scope: Black River mouth, Great Pee Dee extension and actual terminal
correspondence.finding: The lower selected channel remains on mapped Black River below US 701 and joins the distinctly labeled Great Pee Dee River north of Georgetown. The selected line then continues south/southwest on Great Pee Dee River to its endpoint immediately upstream of the US 17 bridge at Georgetown. Waccamaw River and the Intracoastal Waterway are mapped as the separate eastern approach; the selected final reach does not follow them. SCDNR explicitly describes the Black River as ending at its Great Pee Dee confluence, which occurs before this selected endpoint.
correspondence.correspondence: Actual selected terminal and receiving-river continuation inspected in original map pixels. No ocean-mouth extension inferred from the model sea class.

correspondence.finding: The inspected map corridor includes Scape Ore Swamp, Black River Swamp and the broad Dogwood Pond channel complex, along with open meanders and numerous side wetlands. No material named reservoir passage is shown along the selection at this corridor scale. SCDNR calls Black River free-flowing and describes alternation between broad lake-like areas and narrow channels. That prose is confined to Black River and is not a claim that every small headward pool is natural or undammed.
correspondence.correspondence: Mapped waterbody passages distinguished from supporting prose; no new lake name or impoundment history inferred.
